summary: ClockIt gives a small parcel and logistics operation one system for shifts, labor cost, time off and package routes. Since early July 2026, a team of 9 has used it to record about 400 regular shifts.
overview: Name withheld (a small US parcel and logistics operation)
Web portal for admins, managers and workers
Time tracking, payroll export, reports, time off, employee records and route scanning
challenge: A small logistics team needed to see who was working, what each shift cost and where a package belonged. Staff worked morning shifts seven days a week, while route details arrived in Excel files.
The operation needed a system that could:
Let warehouse staff clock in quickly without a complicated login
Show managers who is on shift, on break or off shift in real time
Turn recorded hours into earnings and labor cost without manual calculation
Keep employee, pay and leave information in one place
Find a package's driver, route, stop and order details from a barcode
Before ClockIt, hours were added up by hand and route details stayed in separate spreadsheets. Staff had to search files to find a package’s driver or stop.
solution: Three role-based portals give workers, managers and admins the tools they need. Workers handle their own shift; managers oversee activity; admins manage payroll and records.
ClockIt workflow: workforce and route operations
Worker actions become the shared record behind the Admin views. Route workbooks follow a separate path, turning uploaded files into package lookup.
portals: Clock in and out, take breaks, view daily hours and estimated pay, request time off and manage a personal profile
Oversee staff, activity, reports, routes and time off, without access to payroll
Manage payroll, employee records, time history, routes, reports and scheduling

resultsNotes: ClockIt moved beyond a prototype and became part of the team's daily routine. By November 2, 2026, it had about four months of live shift history.
Regular shift records exclude entries under 1 minute or over 12 hours. They include a small number of test records, so these figures are approximate.

Shifts and breaks now feed one shared time record. Hours support estimated earnings and labour-cost reports, with CSV exports for payroll preparation. Manual corrections show who changed a record, and package scans return the driver, route and stop.
lessons: The review found 32 shifts longer than 12 hours. Several appear to have stayed open until the worker’s next clock-in, showing the need for stronger clock-out checks.
That gap shapes the next stage of the product:
Automatic shift protection: add clock-out reminders, an automatic clock-out and alerts for unusually long shifts.
Cleaner payroll review: flag exceptions before hours reach payroll or labor reports.
Better route coverage: keep route imports current so the scanner stays useful every day.
Fuller leave tracking: show each worker's time-off balance.
Deeper labor insight: record work by operation to compare labor cost across tasks.
